newsitem.title: USA: No chance of Clinton ending UPS strike-White House.
newsitem.headline: No chance of Clinton ending UPS strike-White House.

text.p: White House spokesman Mike McCurry said on Monday he saw "no possibility" of President Bill Clinton intervening to stop the United Parcel Service strike.

"I see no possibility of presidential action on that matter," McCurry told reporters, saying the strike was not likely to meet the standard for presidential action under the Taft-Hartley Act of imperilling the national health or safety.

"It would take passing the Taft-Hartley threshold, which is imperilling the national health or safety, and Taft-Hartley as you know has not been invoked since President Truman, so I don't anticipate presidential action," McCurry added.
McCurry also said Clinton wanted UPS and the Teamsters union to settle their differences and reach an agreement.

"The president concurs in the views of the Secretary of Labour, who encouraged the parties to do what they can to settle their differences and reach a collective bargaining agreement," McCurry said. "But strikes are sometimes a necessary ingredient of the collective bargaining procedure."
The Teamsters union began a strike at UPS early Monday morning, hours after negotiators failed to agree a new contract at the largest U.S. small package carrier.
